To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the excitonic emission energy in UTQWs of CdTe and of CdSe can be continuously tuned in the visible spectral region by modifying the growth temperature, and that the blue shift observed is attributed to a chemical interaction that occurs during growth and that is responsible of the substitution of Cd by Zn atoms at QW–barrier interface.

(i) the exciton emission of ultra-thinned quantum wells (UT-QWs) of CdSe and of CdTe can be tuned in the visible spectral range by modifying the growth temperature of the UT-QWs; and, (ii), the UT-QWs can be described in terms of alloys of Zn 1 − x Cd x Se and Zn 1 −x Cd x Te with high Cd composition.
the growth temperature of UTQW can be employed as a parameter for the fine tuning of the peak emission energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of UTQWs with a thickness of one monolayer (ML) or less.
the growth of UTQWs with a thickness of 1 monolayer (ML) and the study of the optical properties of these UTQWs.

the study of the emission energy of ultra-thin (1 to 2 ML) quantum wells (UTWQs) of CdSe and of CdTe as a function of the substrate temperature during growth, and with the analysis of the results by the consideration of the possible substitution of Cd by Zn at the QW–barrier interfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UTQW can be considered as a ZnCdSe or ZnCdTe alloy with a high Cd content, which is the reason for the blue shift observed in the emission energy with the increase of the growth temperature.
the excitonic emission energy of CdTe and of CdSe ultra-thin quantum well (UTQW) can be fine-tuned by the substrate temperature during the growth.
, the UTQW emission is determined by the average alloy composition of the quantum wells, which is a function of the growth temperature, and not by the thickness of the quantum wells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the excitonic emission energy of UTQWs depends on the growth temperature, which can be used to control the peak emission energy.

, in order to obtain the expected excitonic emission energy of UTQWs, it is necessary to grow at low temperatures, and to take into account the chemical interaction between the UTQWs and the underlying substrate.

the UTQWs of CdTe and Zn 1− y Cd y Te and of CdSe and Zn 1 − y Cd y Se can be considered as the same system, with the same emission energy as a continuous function of thickness, but with different growth temperatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exciton peak position can be tuned by changing the substrate temperature during growth of UTQWs.

the emission energy of UTQWs is not only a function of thickness but also a function of the growth temperature and, consequently, the growth temperature can be used to fine tune the emission energy of ultra-thin QWs of CdSe and of CdTe.
the UTQWs are not pure CdTe or CdSe but alloys of Cd x Zn 1− y Te or Cd x Zn 2− x Se with x, y ∼1.
